terms.heading: Terms
terms.unavailable: The contract terms are unavailable right now.

staking.title: Deposits
staking.yieldRateNote: Simple, not compounding. Yield never folds back into what earns, so what you get depends on your deposit and time, nothing else.
staking.withdrawalsNote: Deposits are not locked. A withdrawal is limited only by what your debt allows: enough has to stay to keep your loan health above the liquidation line.

borrowing.title: Borrowing
borrowing.maxLtvNote: Your borrow limit, as a share of your deposit. A borrow that would cross it is refused rather than allowed and then liquidated.
borrowing.thresholdNote: Where loan health reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible.
borrowing.thresholdNoteGap: Where loan health reaches 1.00 and liquidation becomes possible. The gap above your borrow limit is deliberate: it is the room a loan has to accrue interest before anyone can touch it.
borrowing.kinkNote: Where the borrow rate stops rising gently and starts rising steeply, so lenders are paid to refill a pool that is running dry.

liquidated.title: If you are liquidated
liquidated.closeFactorNote: The most of your debt one liquidation can clear. It limits what a single price dip costs you, and the rest of your deposit survives it.
liquidated.bonusNote: The discount a liquidator takes on the collateral they seize, paid out of your deposit. It is what makes anyone show up to close an underwater loan, which is what keeps the pool solvent.
liquidated.fullNote: Below this loan health, the close-factor cap is lifted and the whole loan can be cleared at once. It’s worked out on chain from the liquidation line and the bonus, not set by anyone. It’s exactly the point where a capped liquidation stops making a loan healthier.

rounds.title: Backing a side
rounds.intro: Odds come from how the pool splits, so the protocol never bets against you.
rounds.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement, so it is already inside the odds you were shown rather than deducted from a win afterwards.
rounds.entryCutoffNote: Entry closes before the round locks so nobody can back a side in the last second against a price they can already see moving.
rounds.minimumPerSideNote: If the smaller side never reaches this, the round is voided and every position is refunded in full. A one-sided pool has nothing to pay winners with.

fees.heading: Protocol earnings
fees.rakeNote: Taken from the losing pool at settlement. A voided round pays no rake at all, since rake is only recorded when a round settles, so a market on a slow feed earns nothing while it keeps voiding.
fees.rakeBound: Capped by the rake collected, not the token balance, so it can never touch money owed to users, including a settled round’s unclaimed winnings.
fees.reservesNote: The protocol's cut of borrower interest, credited when interest accrues into the index rather than when a borrower pays.
fees.reservesBound: Subordinated to suppliers: a withdrawal is refused unless the pool still holds enough cash to meet every supplier claim afterwards. Credited interest that nobody has paid is not withdrawable.
fees.predatesTreasury: This contract was deployed before the stored treasury and has no treasury(). Its withdrawal still takes a destination, so it can only be called from a terminal. That’s the state GHO-40 is about, and it clears on the next deploy.
fees.overAccrued: More than has accrued. The contract would refuse this.

stake.subtitle: It earns while it sits, and it secures everything you borrow

stake.partialExitBlocked: You have a loan against this deposit, so you can only withdraw all of it. The loan is repaid from it first, and the rest comes back to you.
stake.neverLeaves: Your deposit never leaves the vault to secure a loan. Borrowing just puts a claim on it, and the money comes from the lending pool. It keeps earning the whole time. That’s the point: you back your call without cashing out.

borrow.title: Borrow
borrow.subtitle: Borrow against your deposit, or repay what you owe
borrow.needsWallet: Your borrow limit comes from what you have deposited.
borrow.notConfigured: No vault is configured for this network.
borrow.overDebt: That’s more than you owe. Repaying stops at your debt.
borrow.interestNote: Interest adds up every second at the pool’s current rate, so your debt grows on its own between transactions. Borrowing stops at your borrow limit, which sits well below the liquidation line.

lend.title: Lend
lend.subtitle: Fund the pool borrowers draw from, and earn what they pay
lend.notConfigured: No lending pool is configured for this network.
lend.unreadableDetail: The RPC call failed. Anything you’ve supplied is still there. This screen just can’t see it right now.

warnings.exit-blocked: Every token in the pool is out on loan, so nothing can be withdrawn right now. Your balance keeps earning, and cash comes back as borrowers repay.
warnings.exit-limited: More of your balance is out on loan than the pool holds in cash, so you can only withdraw part of it right now. The rest comes back as borrowers repay.
warnings.past-kink: The pool is lent out past its target. That’s why the rate is high, and it’s also why getting out is harder. The steep rate is there to pull lenders in and slow borrowing down.

lend.connectToSupplyDetail: The pool figures above are the same for everyone. Your balance is tied to your address.

pool.heading: The lending pool
pool.borrowersPay: borrowers pay , and that’s where your rate comes from
pool.utilizationNote: Utilization is how much of the pool is out on loan. It’s what you earn, since idle money pays nobody. It’s also what stands between you and the exit, because money that’s lent out isn’t money you can withdraw. Those two facts are the whole decision.

lend.overLiquidity: That’s more than the pool holds in cash. {amount} {symbol} is available right now. The rest of your balance is out on loan and comes back as borrowers repay.
lend.supplyNote: Supplying lowers utilization, and the rate you’re about to earn drops with it. The curve prices scarcity, so more cash makes it cheaper. The figure above is where it lands once your money is in.
lend.withdrawNote: Withdrawing raises utilization for everyone left in the pool, which raises the borrow rate and the supply rate together. Past the target the curve turns steep on purpose.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: Your deposit earns. Borrow against it. Back your call.

landing.headline: Back your call without cashing out.
landing.lede: Most ways to put money behind an opinion make you sell something first. Not here. Your deposit stays put and keeps earning, and you borrow against it to take your position.
landing.readOnly: You don’t need a wallet to look around. Connecting only lets the app read your balance. Nothing moves until you sign.

stake.title: Deposit
stake.body: Put money in the vault and it starts earning right away. It keeps earning through everything that comes after.

borrow.title: Borrow against it
borrow.body: Borrow against your deposit instead of pulling it out. It stays in the vault and keeps working the whole time.

view.title: Back your call
view.body: Pick Yes or No and back it. Odds come from how the pool splits, so there’s no house betting against you.

risks.heading: What happens if you’re wrong
risks.debtStands: <lead>Losing doesn’t cancel the loan.</lead> You borrowed to back that call, and you owe it either way. It’s repaid from your deposit.
risks.interest: <lead>Interest adds up every second.</lead> Leave a loan open and your loan health drifts down on its own, even if prices don’t move.
risks.liquidation: <lead>Drop below 1.00 loan health and anyone can liquidate you.</lead> That’s what keeps the pool solvent, and it comes out of your deposit.
risks.liquidationBonus: <lead>Drop below 1.00 loan health and anyone can liquidate you, taking {bonus} of the collateral they seize.</lead> That’s what keeps the pool solvent, and it comes out of your deposit.
risks.voided: <lead>Rounds can be voided.</lead> If one side never fills, or the price feed can’t be read at settlement, everyone gets their money back. Nobody gets picked as the winner.

landing.testnet: This is a testnet. The token is a free mock you can mint yourself, and every rule above runs on chain. Connect to see your real numbers.

demo.notOwner: Only {owner} can publish on this feed. Without that key the demo market cannot be settled at all.
